1) He only summarizes the formulas and things from the book. He does not begin the topic by first introducing the students to the basic concepts, trying to make them thing out of the box.  By doing so, a student is trapped in the formulas.

2) He is just filling the board with complex equations without even realizing that no one understands what he is doing. He should move through derivations slowly and try to derive things by keeping in mind the level of mindset of students. 

3) He is not making exams in which the students understanding is checked for approximately each area of the course material. He just give random questions, so students who's concepts are good but because they cannot solve those questions get low grades. If the exam covered questions from each area than it would be a fair way of assessing a student's level of understanding. 

4) He should partitioned the questions so that a student has more opportunity to show his level of understanding, that is by not knowing one part he may be able to solve other part which will show that he does know something. This should done be for all physics courses, because exams really mean to assess a student's level of understanding, and it cannot be achieved by just throwing one very difficult question. The exams should take a student through steps.
